description: The dotenv / credentials read leg, on both shells (DEF-718). `write_guard.check_secret_path_access` is the hook-layer replacement for the `Read()` deny rules `init` no longer emits (any `Read()` rule arms a permission prompt bypass mode cannot suppress). Its Bash arm pairs a read verb with a secret-path token in the same statement of the masked command. Until 2026-09-08 the PowerShell tool was read through that bash grammar with the bash roster: `Get-Content .env`, `gc .env`, `type .env` and `Get-Content ~/.aws/credentials` all ALLOWED while `cat .env` denied on both tools -- only because `cat` is a PowerShell alias with the bash spelling (driven 2026-09-07 in the DEF-716 failure-mode pass). Fix: `_PS_SECRET_READ_VERBS`, the bash roster's classes spelled for PowerShell (viewers, byte dumpers, record readers, copiers, the dot-source), consumed by `_ps_secret_read_targets` over the scan text with PowerShell's own separator set (`=` included: an assignment RUNS its right-hand side), colon-bound switch values and comma arrays as operands; `check_secret_path_access` dispatches on the tool name. The two rosters are pinned to each other class for class. Boundary, unchanged: a grep-shaped search of the file (`grep KEY .env`, `Select-String -Path .env`) is not a read verb on either shell; a runtime-assembled path is out of scope; a `foreach ($l in Get-Content .env)` head is a declared miss.
